classificationNotes: A natural suid expedition family centered on predictable charge lanes, bracing, displacement, and route creation.
visualConstants: Every form keeps a low four-legged boar body, cloven hooves, mobile snout, raised bristles, short tail, and visible tusk roots.
Tier escalation uses tusk geometry, neck mass, shoulder callus, scars, and bristle profile rather than humanoid equipment.
Charge direction remains readable through hoof placement, lowered head angle, tusk contact, dust, and the alignment of the spine.
escalationAxis: A short straight charge becomes a braced line-breaker, curved furrow specialist, formation-opening champion, and three-lane sovereign stampede.

constructionDimensions: Bristles, mud, hide, tusks, hooves, saliva, scars, and dust remain ordinary and materially distinct.
Charge weight reads through hoof trenches, shoulder compression, and displaced soil.
normal.counterplaySignal: The pawing hoof, loaded hind legs, buried inside tusk, hooked obstacle, or scored stampede lane remains plainly visible.
forbidden: Elemental glow or unexplained magical anatomy
Manufactured barding that hides the animal's shoulder and spine

constructionDimensions: Bristle tips char and flare backward from acceleration while ember seams remain localized to tusk roots and shoulder calluses.
Hoof sparks, smoke trails, and brief burning furrows reveal charge direction and cool after impact.
fire.counterplaySignal: The loaded shoulder and tusk root brighten before the charge, then expose a cooling seam on collision.

constructionDimensions: Packed soil and mineral plates reinforce the forehead, shoulders, hooves, and tusk bases while hide and bristles remain dominant.
Charges peel up coherent furrows and detached stones that follow the exact route.
earth.counterplaySignal: A pale fracture seam opens at the planted hoof or outside shoulder when the Boar commits to turning or bracing.
forbidden: Random floating rocks unrelated to the charge route

constructionDimensions: Bristles flatten into directional vanes and tusk-edge pressure lines show the future lane while the opaque body remains heavy.
Dust, leaves, and compression wakes trace straight or curved charge geometry before impact.
wind.counterplaySignal: The pressure wake narrows to the planted hindquarters before release and collapses at the flank afterward.
forbidden: Turbulence that hides the route instead of explaining it

constructionDimensions: Wet bristles stream backward over solid hide while pressurized water gathers along tusks and shoulder channels.
Charges throw narrow wakes and coherent bow waves whose curve matches the authored lane.
water.counterplaySignal: The tusk channel drains and the waterlogged outside leg sags after commitment, preserving the flank punish.
forbidden: Opaque splash that hides hooves or tusk direction

forms.battlefieldDuty: Make one short straight charge that cannot turn after a single scrape.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach the simplest charge tell and reward a lateral sidestep rather than backward retreat.
forms.signatureMechanic: Two-Scrape Charge: one forehoof paws twice before the Hog launches along its fixed head line.
forms.telegraph: The forehoof scrapes twice and the head lowers between the shoulders.
forms.counterplay: Sidestep the fixed lane and punish the exposed flank during its stop.
forms.visualDelta: Compact wild hog with raised bristles, short tusks, low ordinary body, and clean unscarred flanks.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Brace inside narrow ground and drive targets out of cover with a long committed charge.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to turn a dangerous lane into a collision by reading the full brace.
forms.signatureMechanic: Tunnel Brace: both hind legs lock before a long charge that gains power in narrow terrain but cannot evade obstacles.
forms.telegraph: Both hind hooves settle and dust funnels backward along the future lane.
forms.counterplay: Leave the lane or make the Boar collide with solid terrain, exposing its stunned forehead and flank.
forms.visualDelta: Thick-necked cave boar with worn forehead, longer tusks, mud-packed coat, and reinforced shoulder callus.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Bristle Hogs make short probes that encourage the target to enter the Tunnel Boar's longer lane.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Cut a curved furrow whose route controls the next charge and throws debris outward.
forms.teachingGoal: Introduce a specialist whose charge can curve but must first draw its complete route into the ground.
forms.signatureMechanic: Plow Curve: the inside tusk remains buried while the Razorback scores a visible curved path for its next charge.
forms.telegraph: The inside tusk stays in the soil and back bristles ripple along the future curve.
forms.counterplay: Cross the furrow before launch or strike the rooted outside leg while the curve is being cut.
forms.visualDelta: Tall sail-like bristle ridge, asymmetric plow tusk, and visibly overbuilt shoulder on the cutting side.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Bristle Hogs rush across the outside edge while Tunnel Boars threaten the straight escape from the curve.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Hook barriers, rotate them into new lanes, and signal lesser Boars to charge through the opening.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to protect or release movable cover before the Boar family weaponizes it.
forms.signatureMechanic: Tusker's Gate: one tusk hooks a barrier while the neck rotates it, creating a new family charge route.
forms.telegraph: The neck twists beneath the hooked object and the free tusk points down the intended lane.
forms.counterplay: Release or destroy the object, or stagger the planted rear leg before the rotation locks.
forms.visualDelta: Towering scarred boar with splayed paired tusks, chipped forehead shield, heavy neck folds, and a low lateral brace.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Lower Boars immediately use the opened route, but collide or scatter if the gate is released before their charge.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Create three successive stampede lanes before personally collapsing the remaining safe route.
forms.teachingGoal: Test straight lanes, collision terrain, curved furrows, and rotated barriers in one readable stampede puzzle.
forms.signatureMechanic: Three-Lane Stampede: each tusk scores a lane and assigns Bristle Hogs, Tunnel Boars, or Razorbacks to lead it before Old Tusk takes the final gap.
forms.telegraph: The mane rises from tail to skull and the assigned lane leader stamps once inside its scored route.
forms.counterplay: Interrupt a lane leader to preserve its gap, then redirect Old Tusk into the disabled route's obstacle.
forms.visualDelta: Enormous ancient boar with one broken outer tusk, root-tangled mane, layered shoulder scars, and an extremely low unstoppable silhouette.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Each lower form leads one route type while the War Tusker reshapes cover; removing a leader permanently preserves that lane during the boss phase.
